spec.name: Customer & Orders Internal App (rep 4)
spec.stack: Our usual web stack — Next.js (React/TypeScript) frontend + NestJS (TypeScript) backend — with Supabase providing authentication and file storage instead of our usual auth/storage. Local development only; NOT deployed in this run.
spec.description: OBJECTIVE: Build a SMALL internal web app (this is rep 4) that lists our customers and their orders, for internal staff use. STACK: Use our usual web stack (Next.js frontend + NestJS backend, TypeScript throughout) — EXCEPT authentication and file storage, which MUST use Supabase (Supabase Auth + Supabase Storage), a platform we have NOT used before and must set up/learn for this project. DELIVERABLE SCOPE: internal directory UI that lists customers and, per customer, their orders; staff must authenticate (via Supabase Auth) to access it; any file attachments/documents use Supabase Storage. FOLDERS: build entirely inside this project's own folder (its localPath) — create frontend/ and backend/ subfolders there; do NOT scaffold anything at the Odin app repo root and do NOT touch any other project. INTEGRATIONS: Supabase (Auth + Storage) is the only mandated external integration; wire credentials via environment variables only — never commit secrets. Customer/order data source: start from a local database (seed/mock data acceptable for a small internal app) unless the owner points to a real source. DEPLOY: DO NOT deploy this yet — stop at a working local build. No VM sync, no firewall changes, no production touch in this run.
features: Supabase Auth login/logout for internal staff (session-gated access to the whole app)
Customer list view (searchable/sortable list of customers)
Customer detail view showing that customer's orders
Orders list per customer (order id, date, status, total, line items)
File attachments per customer/order stored in Supabase Storage (upload + view/download)
Backend API (NestJS) exposing customers/orders endpoints, protected by Supabase-issued auth
Local seed/mock data for customers and orders so the app runs end-to-end without a live data source
Environment-based config for Supabase keys (no secrets committed)

features.name: Role-based access (admin vs read-only staff)
features.why: Internal customer/order data is sensitive; Supabase Auth supports roles/RLS cheaply and limits who can upload/delete files — worth adding before real data goes in.

features.name: Supabase Row-Level Security (RLS) policies
features.why: Since Supabase owns auth, enforcing RLS on the data tables (not just the API) gives defense-in-depth so a leaked anon key can't read all customers.

members.name: Designer
members.why: Only if the owner wants a polished internal UI; a small staff tool can ship with plain functional styling, so not auto-staffed.
